claims.claim: A navy captain reported approximately sixty feet of serpent (in addition to the head above water)
claims.quote: The serpent was witnessed to have been swimming with 1.2 m (4 feet) of its head above the water and they believed that there was another 18 m (60 feet) of the creature in the sea.

claims.claim: The sighting was made from HMS Daedalus, between the Cape of Good Hope and St Helena
claims.quote: The vessel sighted what they named as an enormous serpent between the Cape of Good Hope and St Helena.

claims.claim: The captain and several officers signed the report
claims.quote: On 6 August 1848 Captain M'Quhae of HMS Daedalus and several of his officers and crew (en route to St Helena) saw a sea serpent which was subsequently reported (and debated) in The Times.

claims.claim: M'Quhae wrote that had the creature been a man of his acquaintance he should have easily recognized his features with the naked eye
claims.quote: Captain M'Quhae also said that "[The creature] passed rapidly, but so close under our lee quarter, that had it been a man of my acquaintance I should have easily recognized his features with the naked eye."

claims.claim: Seven crew members said the creature remained in view for around twenty minutes
claims.quote: According to seven members of the crew, it remained in view for around twenty minutes.

claims.claim: An editor suggested the Captain had read the old Dane and was copying him
claims.quote: One might fancy the galant Captain had read the old Dane, and was copying him

claims.claim: The description included dark brown colour, white about the throat, and the neck clothed as if by a horse's mane or a bunch of sea-weed
claims.quote: when he tells of the dark brown colour and white about the throat, and the neck clothed as if by a horse's mane or a bunch of sea-weed

claims.claim: The Literary Gazette called these the exact words of Pontoppidan (the historian)
claims.quote: the exact words of the historian

claims.claim: Sailors threatened by a sea serpent threw large objects such as paddles or shovels overboard in the serpent's path, hoping it would take the object and leave
claims.quote: Sailors threatened by a sea serpent were said to have thrown large objects such as paddles or shovels overboard in the path of the serpent, hoping that the serpent would take the object and leave without destroying the ship.

claims.claim: Sailors reported that sea serpents would destroy ships by wrapping them in coils of their body and pulling them underwater
claims.quote: a number of reports were made by sailors at the time that sea serpents would destroy ships by wrapping the ship in coils of their body and pulling it underwater

claims.claim: In 1734 the creature raised itself so that its head reached above the main-top (top of the mainmast)
claims.quote: On the 6th of July, 1734, there appeared a very large and frightful sea monster, which raised itself so high out of the water that its head reached above our main-top (top of the mainmast).

claims.claim: Hans Egede recorded the sighting in his journal in connection with Greenland
claims.quote: Rev. Hans Egede,  a Dano-Norwegian clergyman who was an early explorer and surveyor of Greenland, gave an 18th-century description of a sea serpent witnessed by his party. In his journal he wrote:

claims.claim: Egede described a long sharp snout, spouting water like a whale, and the tail turned up above the surface a whole ship-length from the head
claims.quote: It had a long, sharp snout, and spouted water like a whale; and very broad flappers. ... and then turned its tail up above the surface, a whole ship-length from the head.

claims.claim: Henry Lee explained the Egede sea-serpent as a giant squid
claims.quote: Lee proposed a rational explanation that this sea-serpent was a misapprehended sighting of what was actually the exposed head and one tentacle of a giant squid

claims.claim: Evolutionary biologist Gary J. Galbreath contends the Daedalus crew saw a sei whale
claims.quote: Evolutionary biologist Gary J. Galbreath contends that what the crew of Daedalus saw was a sei whale.

claims.claim: The oarfish shown was 16 ft long, washed ashore in Bermuda in 1860, and was originally described as a sea serpent
claims.quote: Description: Oarfish that washed ashore on a Bermuda beach in 1860. The animal was 16 ft long and was originally described as a sea serpent.

claims.claim: The sighting took place on 6 August 1848
claims.quote: On 6 August 1848 Captain M'Quhae of HMS Daedalus and several of his officers and crew (en route to St Helena) saw a sea serpent

claims.claim: The creature passed close under the ship's lee quarter
claims.quote: [The creature] passed rapidly, but so close under our lee quarter

claims.claim: Four feet of head was above the water
claims.quote: The serpent was witnessed to have been swimming with 1.2 m (4 feet) of its head above the water

claims.claim: Another officer thought the creature was more of a lizard than a serpent
claims.quote: Another officer wrote that the creature was more of a lizard than a serpent.

claims.claim: The sighting was reported and debated in The Times
claims.quote: saw a sea serpent which was subsequently reported (and debated) in The Times

claims.claim: Pontoppidan's description was written about a century before 1848
claims.quote: Norwegian Bishop Erik Pontoppidan (1698–1764) did not disbelieve the existence of sea serpents themselves

claims.claim: Giant oarfish are presumed responsible for some sea serpent sightings
claims.quote: Due to their size, elongated bodies, and undulating swimming pattern, giant oarfish are also presumed to be responsible for some sea serpent sightings.

claims.claim: A 2016 paper attributed a significant number of sightings to whales entangled in fishing gear and maritime debris
claims.quote: R.L. France proposed in a 2016 paper for the International Journal of Maritime History that a significant number of sea serpent sightings, including nineteenth century accounts of serpents attacking whales, were due to the misidentification of whales entangled in fishing gear and maritime debris.

claims.claim: In 1845 a 115-foot "sea serpent" skeleton was exhibited in New York by Albert C. Koch
claims.quote: In 1845, a 35 m (115 ft) long skeleton allegedly belonging to an extinct sea serpent was exhibited in New York City by Albert C. Koch.

claims.claim: The anatomist Jeffries Wyman examined the skeleton and found it composed of bones of several different animals, including an extinct whale
claims.quote: Wyman declared that the skull of the animal had to be mammalian in origin, and that the skeleton was composed of bones of several different animals, including an extinct species of whale.
